content:
Newly elected Wisconsin Rep. Rebecca Cooke celebrated the end of her freshman orientation in Washington, D.C., with both a photo and some Grade-A trolling.

Cooke worked as a waitress at a farm-to-table restaurant before beating Republican Derrick Van Orden during this month’s midterms.

She decided the best way to commemorate the visit was by taking a photo of the ceiling of the Capitol dome while lying on the floor.

That’s a wrap on freshmen orientation! Commemorated my time here by taking a photo of the Capitol dome. No one yelled at me...

Cooke’s decision to take this particular photo was a clear provocation of Van Orden, who was accused in July 2023 of shouting at a group of Senate pages for taking similar photos of the interior of the U.S. Capitol dome.

“Wake the f**k up, you little s**ts. … What the f**k are you all doing? Get the f**k out of here. You are defiling the space you [pieces of s**t],” Van Orden allegedly told the group of teenagers.

But you have to give Van Orden credit for consistency. He brought all of his “get off my lawn” energy in his response to Cooke’s post:

Great way to start.

This disgraces the memory of the wounded Union Soldiers that died on this floor during the Civil War.

Petulant children need harsh words.

But if Van Orden expected a groundswell of support for his fervent defense of the sanctity of the Capitol, he was sadly mistaken.

Many people on social media noted that Van Orden used leftover campaign funds to attend rallies on Jan. 6, 2021, intended to stop Congress from certifying Joe Biden’s victory.

Van Orden claimed in an op-ed published in the La Crosse Tribune days after the attack that, yes, he was at the Capitol on Jan. 6, but left “when it became clear that a protest had become a mob.”

Many people reacted to Van Orden’s post to Cooke by pointing out the contradiction between getting butt-hurt over someone taking a photo while lying on the floor of the Capitol versus, say, supporting an insurrection that caused damage and destruction.
